title: When Booking Stops and How an Event Services Agreement Ends
content:
Booking is stopped on a Private Event & Banquet Services agreement when arrears pass the credit hold threshold or when a required certificate of event insurance lapses, and it restarts once the balance is settled or the certificate replaced.

## The states in which a hold or a closure is worked

A hold or a closure is only worked while the agreement stands active, on hold or closed, and never on a proposal, which is withdrawn instead. That state is read from the company's records against the agreement's own reference, together with the deposit money the records show standing on it.

## Events already in the diary

Events already confirmed when a hold goes on are still delivered, because the client has paid deposits against them and the venue has held the date.

## Ending the agreement

1. Only the client may end an event services agreement, and the desk records the request for the client to confirm rather than closing the agreement on their word alone.
2. Notice to end the agreement is the number of calendar days printed against the package, and every confirmed event inside that notice period is delivered or cancelled on the ordinary cancellation terms before the agreement closes.
3. An agreement is not closed while deposit money is still held against an unserved booking; the deposit is returned or applied first.

## The minimum number of events a year

Where the client has not reached the minimum number of events a year printed against the package, no shortfall charge falls due, since the package prices each event on its own.

## Points of judgement

*On an agreement carrying deposit money.* Deposit money standing against a booking that has been neither delivered nor cancelled stops the agreement closing until that money is returned or applied, whatever notice has run.

*On a proposal the client no longer wants.* A proposal is withdrawn rather than held or closed, so neither the notice period nor the deposit condition arises on it.
